key_insight: Eigenvalue-based neural constitutive models jointly learn yield surfaces and evolution laws for isotropic elastoplasticity while enforcing thermodynamic consistency, including non-associative flow.
engineering_relevance: The approach supports flexible material modeling from stress–strain data and deployment in finite element boundary-value simulations.
method: Enforce isotropy and convexity through permutation-invariant spectral representations.
Construct non-associative yield functions by adding a jointly learned term to a convex flow potential.
Train through a backward-Euler return map using implicit differentiation with eigenvalue-degeneracy safeguards.
evidence_signal: Evaluations reproduce known constitutive models, learn from full-field finite element stress–strain data and homogenized foam responses, and demonstrate plane-stress finite element simulations.
watch_item: Implementation requires careful differentiation near repeated eigenvalues; the stated scope is rate-independent, isotropic elastoplasticity.
paper_title: Thermodynamically consistent neural constitutive models for elastoplasticity via eigen-representations
